nestedAgents.text:
No. SQLite WAL requires all database processes on the same host; it does not work over a network filesystem.

- Official source: https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html
- Decisive passage: “All processes using a database must be on the same host computer; WAL does not work over a network filesystem.”

rows.finding: SQLite's Online Backup API permits a live source database to be backed up while other connections read and write it; the destination remains in a write transaction for the backup duration.

support.title: Online Backup API.
support.passage: SQLite holds a write transaction open on the destination database file for the duration of the backup operation. The source database is read-locked only while it is being read; it is not locked continuously for the entire backup operation. Thus, the backup may be performed on a live source database without preventing other database connections from reading or writing to the source database while the backup is underway.

rows.method: Documented API locking semantics, not a workload measurement. Applies to backups made through SQLite's Online Backup API.
rows.comparability: This is a database-file/API backup mechanism, whereas PostgreSQL pg_basebackup is a physical cluster backup; no throughput comparison follows.
